caption: I guessed the vending machine was costing me R300. It's R750, and I'm only in my first year of earning anything at all. What did your first payslip actually go on?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R11 200
p/m stipend
Living in Benoni
slides.body:
Male, 19
Single, lives with parents
Job: First-year apprentice fitter and turner
Net stipend: R11 200 p/m

slides.title: Board to parents
slides.includes: Covers my share of groceries and electricity at home
slides.body: My dad wouldn't take a cent from me until I actually got paid. Now he won't take less than this.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the TVET college two days a week, workshop the rest
slides.body: Two different routes, two different fares, every single week.

slides.title: Tools & PPE
slides.includes: Steel-cap boots, overalls, replacing a socket set that grew legs
slides.body: Nobody tells you an apprenticeship has its own running costs before you've even qualified.

slides.title: Takeaways & vending machine
slides.includes: The machine at the workshop, garage pies, Friday KFC with the other apprentices
slides.body: I guessed R300. It's R750. Turns out that machine takes cards now, which is worse for me.

slides.title: Airtime & data
slides.includes: The college portal, WhatsApp, calling my mom when I miss the taxi

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Funeral policy, a stokvel with two other apprentices, clothing account, savings toward my own place, extra for my mom's electricity
slides.body: Five small things I'd never added up before this. Together they're more than my board.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R11 200. That's about R27 a day, and this is only my first year of earning a proper wage at all.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where my stipend went
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The vending machine and takeaways alone came to R750 — I would have guessed R300.

No bank login needed.
